# `Bytes`

## `empty`

```ipe
empty : Bytes
```

The empty byte buffer (zero bytes).

## `length`

```ipe
length : Bytes -> Int
```

The number of bytes in the buffer.

## `isEmpty`

```ipe
isEmpty : Bytes -> Bool
```

True when the buffer contains no bytes.

## `fromString`

```ipe
fromString : String -> Bytes
```

UTF-8-encode a Ipe `String` into a `Bytes` buffer.

Every Ipe `String` is valid UTF-8, so this conversion is total (never
fails).  To go the other way, use `toString`.

## `toString`

```ipe
toString : Bytes -> Maybe String
```

UTF-8-decode a `Bytes` buffer into a Ipe `String`.

Returns `Just s` when the entire buffer is valid UTF-8, `Nothing`
otherwise.  Use `Maybe.withDefault` when you need a fallback string.

## `fromHex`

```ipe
fromHex : String -> Maybe Bytes
```

Decode a hexadecimal string into bytes.

Accepts both lowercase and uppercase hex digits.  Returns `Nothing` when
the input has an odd length or contains any character outside `[0-9a-fA-F]`.

## `toHex`

```ipe
toHex : Bytes -> String
```

Hex-encode a byte buffer (lowercase output, two hex digits per byte).

## `fromBase64`

```ipe
fromBase64 : String -> Maybe Bytes
```

Standard (RFC 4648) base-64 decode.

Returns `Nothing` on invalid padding or non-base-64 characters.

## `toBase64`

```ipe
toBase64 : Bytes -> String
```

Standard (RFC 4648) base-64 encode.

## `append`

```ipe
append : Bytes -> Bytes -> Bytes
```

Concatenate two byte buffers.

## `slice`

```ipe
slice : Int -> Int -> Bytes -> Bytes
```

`slice start end bytes` — return bytes in the half-open interval
`[start, end)`, where negative indices count from the end of the buffer
(mirrors `String.slice`).

Out-of-range indices are clamped to the buffer boundaries; `start >= end`
(after clamping) returns the empty buffer.
